text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Group of non-governmental organisations and individuals propose former Nigerian foreign minister Major-General Joseph Garba for post of U.N. Secretary-General, but without backing from military government.
- Oil distributors campaign for increase in their current 1.30 naira profit margin from fuel pump price of 11 naira per litre.
- Plans concluded to harmonise in next year's budget multiple taxes paid by private businesses, government sources say.
- Rescue operations at mangrove lagoon where a Nigerian airliner crashed last month killing all 142 on board cost 20 million naira, sources at the airline's insurers say.
- Manufacturers with huge pile of unsold stock take goods to streets to sell as part of measures taken to dispose of them.
- Nigeria spends about 16 billion naira to import 600,000 out of its required 800,000 metric tonnes of fish yearly, Lanre Talabi, president of the Fisheries Society of Nigeria says.

- Heads of the five registered political parties, representatives of non-governmental organisations and the opposition plan to attend seminar on Nigeria's transition programme in the United States next week.
- Newly-inaugurated 172-man committee on the economic programme Vision 2010 plan two-day workshop in the capital Abuja to deliberate on charting an economic masterplan for Nigeria.
